source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: Then{H227} Yeshua{H3442} was taken{H3947} by the Spirit{H7307} of Holiness{H6944} to the wilderness{H4057}, to be tested{H5254} by the Satan{H7854}.

one_way_hebrew: להתנסות (H5254) — the Akedah's verb (והאלהים נסה את אברהם, Gen 22:1) and the wilderness-test of Deut 8:2 (למען ענתך לנסתך — 'to humble you, to TEST you' — forty years in the wilderness). The forty-day trial replays Israel's, and every answer given in this chapter (vv. 4, 7, 10) is quoted from Deut 6-8 — the chapters about that very testing.
השטן — ha-Satan with the article, the accuser of Job 1-2 and Zech 3: a Hebrew office-name, not a Greek proper noun; v. 10 will gloss it with the church's form.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק תשיעי (Perek 9) begins here (the transcription's heading misprints פרפ for פרק).
Howard's apparatus (4:1): הקדוש] הקודש B.

verses.translation: And he fasted{H6684} forty days{H3117} and forty{H705} nights{H3915}, and afterwards he hungered{H7456}.

one_way_hebrew: Forty days and forty nights — Moshe's fast on the mountain, verbatim (Exod 34:28, ארבעים יום וארבעים לילה לחם לא אכל) and Eliyahu's journey on one meal (1 Kgs 19:8). The ms writes the first forty as the letter-numeral מ״ and the second as the word וארבעים — a scribe's living hand, not a translator's mechanical equivalence.
textual_notes: The ms writes מ״ (the numeral 40) and ואח״כ (abbreviation of ואחר כך, 'and afterwards').

verses.translation: The tester{H5254} drew near{H7126} and said{H559} to him: If you are the son{H1121} of Elohim{H430}, say{H559} that these{H428} stones{H68} turn into{H7725} bread{H3899}.

one_way_hebrew: המנסה — 'the TESTER': named from the same root as v. 1's נסיון; the Hebrew keeps trial and trier on one root (Greek ὁ πειράζων does too — because it translates this idiom).

אבנים... לחם — stones and bread: the stones/sons pun of 3:9 still hangs in the air (אבנים/בנים), and the taunt אם בן אלקים אתה picks up its בן. First occurrence of אלקים in the chapter — the ms's reverent ק-spelling (see 1:23).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (4:3): מקרב] ויקרב ABDEFG; אלקים] אלהים A, אלוה G; לו omitted in DEF; האלה] האלו A.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} and said{H559} to him: It is written{H3789}: Not by the bread{H3899} alone{H905} — and so on.

one_way_hebrew: The answer is Deut 8:3 cited by its opening words and broken off with וגו׳ ('etc.'): the hearer — and the reader — completes כי על כל מוצא פי יהוה יחיה האדם from memory. Greek Matthew must write the whole verse out. Ms D completes it exactly so (יחיה האדם כי על כל מוצא פי ה׳), ABEFG add יחיה האדם. Scripture-by-incipit is this text's habit (2:18; 3:12; 4:6) — the fingerprint of a Hebrew book among readers who know the Tanakh by heart.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (4:4): לבדו] + יחיה האדם ABEFG; D adds יחיה האדם כי על כל מוצא פי ה; כתוב] + הוא ABCDEF; לו] לך A.

verses.translation: Then{H227} the Satan{H7854} took{H3947} him to the Holy{H6944} City{H5892} and stood him{H5975} on the highest{H1364} place{H4725} in all{H3605} the Sanctuary{H4720},

one_way_hebrew: עיר הקדוש — 'the city of the Holy' (Isa 52:1 עיר הקדש; Neh 11:1), and המקדש — the mikdash, the Torah's word for the holy precinct (as at 24:1): the pinnacle is 'the highest place in all the MIKDASH,' not a Greek πτερύγιον ('little wing') of a ἱερόν.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (4:5): שבכל] שבבית G.

verses.translation: and said{H559} to him: If you are Elohim{H430}, leap{H1801} down{H4295} — and so forth — for he will command{H6680} his messengers{H4397} for you, to keep you{H8104} in all{H3605} your ways{H1870}, etc.

one_way_hebrew: The Satan quotes Ps 91:11 in its own consonants — כי מלאכיו יצוה לך לשמרך בכל דרכיך — and the text breaks off with וגו׳, leaving Ps 91:12 unquoted (Greek Matthew quotes on: 'in their hands they shall bear thee up'). Ms A completes the psalm exactly — על כפים ישאונך פן תיגף באבן רגליך — and BDEF add the same with וכו׳. Even the devil cites Scripture by incipit in this text.
דלג (H1801) — 'leap': the leaping of Song 2:8 (מדלג על ההרים); a concrete Hebrew verb where Greek has βάλε σεαυτὸν κάτω ('throw yourself down').
greek_deviations: The base text reads 'If you are ELOHIM' — not 'son of Elohim' as at v. 3: the second temptation escalates the taunt. Mss ABDEF read בן אלים and G בן אלוה ('son of El / Eloah'), assimilating back toward the Greek; Howard's English keeps the base: 'If you are God, jump down.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (4:6): אלקים] בן אלים ABDEF, בן אלוה G; אליו] לו EF; וכ׳] וכתיב ABDEFG; דרכיך] + על כפים ישאונך פן תיגף באבן רגליך A, + על כפים ישאונך וכו׳ BDEF.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} him a second time{H8145}: You shall not test{H5254} YHWH{H3068} your Elohim{H430}.

one_way_hebrew: Deut 6:16 in its own words — לא תנסו את יהוה אלהיכם, here in the singular — and the verb is the chapter's root נסה a third time: the tested one forbids testing. The Hebrew chapter runs on one root where Greek needs πειράζω/ἐκπειράζω.
textual_notes: First ה״ of the chapter (the ms circumlocution for the Name; see 1:22).
Howard's apparatus (4:7): שנית] + כן כתיב A, + ג״כ כתיב BDEFG ('it is likewise written'); את] + שם BEF ('you shall not test the NAME of YHWH'); ויען] ויאמר G; אלקיך] אלהיך A.

verses.translation: And the Satan{H7854} carried{H5375} him to an exceedingly{H3966} high{H1364} mountain{H2022} and showed him{H7200} all{H3605} the kingdoms{H4467} of the earth{H776} and their glory{H3519},

one_way_hebrew: וישא — the Satan 'CARRIED him' (נשא), the vision-transport verb of Ezek 8:3 (ותשא אתי רוח). And the mountain-showing is the Pisgah scene: Deut 34:1-4, where YHWH takes Moshe up the mountain 'and showed him (ויראהו!) all the land.' The tempter apes the mountain-vision God gave Moshe — same verb, same staging — offering what is not his to give.
textual_notes: The transcription duplicates v. 9's clause (ויאמר לו כל אלה אתן לך אם תפרע אלי) at the end of this verse; the scan shows v. 8 ending at וכבודם — corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (4:8): ויראהו] + את G.

verses.translation: and he said{H559} to him: All{H3605} these{H428} I will give{H5414} you, if you bare your head{H6544} to me.

greek_deviations: 'If you BARE YOUR HEAD to me' — תפרע (H6544), the verb of unbinding the head (Lev 10:6, ראשיכם אל תפרעו; 21:10 — the very act the Torah forbids the priests): a concrete gesture of submission and homage. Greek has 'if you fall down and worship me' (πεσὼν προσκυνήσῃς). Mss assimilate toward the Greek — A תכרע ('bow'), BDEFG תכרע ותשתחוה ('bow and worship') — but the base's strange, priestly-law idiom is the reading no one would invent from the Greek; Howard renders it 'if you bare your head to me.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (4:9): תפרע] תכרע A, תכרע ותשתחוה BDEFG.

verses.translation: Then{H227} Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} him: Go{H1980}, Satan{H7854} — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, Satanas — for thus it is written{H3789}: YHWH{H3068} I will pray to{H6419}, and him alone{H905} you shall serve{H5647}.

one_way_hebrew: The scribe glosses even השטן with the church's form: בלעז שאטאנאס. Greek Σατανᾶς is itself a transliteration OF the Hebrew שטן — yet here it is the Greek form that must be explained as the foreign word. The gloss only runs one direction: out of Hebrew, toward readers who know church vocabulary (as at 1:16; 2:11; 3:7; 24:14-15).
greek_deviations: The Deut 6:13 quotation is bent into confession: את ה״ אתפלל — 'YHWH I will PRAY TO' (first person), where Deuteronomy has תירא ('you shall fear') and Greek προσκυνήσεις ('you shall worship'). The answerer takes the command into his own mouth. Mss ADEFG level it back to the imperative התפלל.
translation_notes: The transcription reads בלעג; the scan reads בלעז, corrected here. The printed שאטאנאס carries vowel points; stripped.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (4:10): אתפלל] התפלל ADEFG; בלעז] לעז ADEFG; שאטאנאס] spelled variously in the mss (שטאנש AC, שאטאנש B, etc.).

verses.translation: Then{H227} the Satan{H7854} left{H5800} him; and behold{H2009}, messengers{H4397} drew near{H7126} to him and ministered to him.

one_way_hebrew: The scene closes the Eliyahu frame opened by the forty-day fast (v. 2): a מלאך touched Elijah and fed him in the wilderness (1 Kgs 19:5-7). מלאכים — sent ones, messengers (never 'a winged species'); the same word carried the Name's message in chs. 1-2.
translation_notes: וישרפוהו — the base ms reads 'and they BURNED him' (a copyist's פ for ת); all other mss read וישרתוהו ('and they MINISTERED to him' — שרת, the priestly service verb, Exod 28:35), which the sense requires; Howard prints '(ministered).' The translation follows the sense; the words preserve the ms.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (4:11): וישרפוהו] וישרתוהו ABCDEFG.

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961} in those{H1992} days{H3117}, Yeshua{H3442} heard{H8085} that Yochanan{H3110} had been delivered{H4560} into prison{H612}, and he went{H1980} to Gilgal{H1537}.

greek_deviations: 'He went to GILGAL' (הגלגל) — where Greek has Galilee — the second time the base text reads Gilgal for Galilee (2:22); ms B again normalizes to הגליל. Once is a slip; twice is a text. Gilgal is the Jordan-side camp of Yehoshua (Josh 4:19-5:10), the place of entry into the land — a reading with its own geography, not a translator's error.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק עשירי (Perek 10) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (4:12): הגלגל] הגליל B.

verses.translation: And he passed by{H5674} Nazaral and dwelt{H7931} in Kefar{H3723} Nachum{H5151} Raithah — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, Maritima — at the edge{H7097} of the land{H776} of Zevulun{H2074},

one_way_hebrew: כפר נחום — in Hebrew the town's name is transparent: kefar (village, H3723) + Nachum ('comfort', the prophet's name); Greek Καφαρναούμ is an opaque transliteration of it.

The gloss לעז מאריטמה is Latin — maritima, 'by the sea' — exactly what Greek Matthew says of Capernaum (παραθαλασσίαν). A Hebrew text carrying Latin glosses for its readers (with מי״רא 2:11, ליבי״ל ריפודייו 5:31) is a text at home among Hebrew readers in a Latin-speaking land — not a translation made from the Greek.
greek_deviations: The verse ends at 'the land of Zevulun' — no 'and Naphtali' (Greek: ἐν ὁρίοις Ζαβουλὼν καὶ Νεφθαλίμ); the quotation in v. 15 supplies both tribes.
translation_notes: ראיתה [?] — an obscure word: Howard reads it as part of the name ('Capernaum-Raithah'), its meaning carried by the לעז gloss ('by the sea'). The variants (ראתה B, מרתה D, רמתה FG) show the copyists themselves no longer understood it. The transcription reads ואיתה; the scan reads ראיתה, corrected here — flagged uncertain as to sense, not as to letters.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (4:13): נאזראל] נזראל BD, נאזרתאל F; ראיתה] ראתה B, מרתה D, רמתה FG; לעז] בלעז BG, omit D; the לעז word is spelled variously (מרטימה, מאראטימה, etc.). The printed מאריטמה carries vowel points; stripped.

verses.translation: to establish{H6965} what Yeshayahu{H3470} the prophet{H5030} said:

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (4:14): ישעיהו] ישעיה ABEF; הנביא omitted in FG.

verses.translation: Toward the land{H776} of Zevulun{H2074} and toward the land of Naphtali{H5321}, the way{H1870} of the sea{H3220}, beyond{H5676} the Jordan{H3383}, Galil{H1551} of the nations{H1471}:

one_way_hebrew: Isa 8:23 in Isaiah's own consonants — ארצה זבלון וארצה נפתלי... דרך הים עבר הירדן גליל הגוים — including the archaic directional ־ה of ארצה ('LANDWARD of Zevulun'), which Greek Matthew flattens to γῆ Ζαβουλών ('land of Zebulun'). No back-translator recovers a locative he-suffix from a Greek nominative; the text is quoting Isaiah, not reconstructing him.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (4:15): את omitted in AEF.

verses.translation: The people{H5971} who walk{H1980} in darkness{H2822} have seen{H7200} a great{H1419} light{H216}; the dwellers{H3427} in the land{H776} of the shadow of death{H6757} — a light has shined{H5050} upon them.

one_way_hebrew: Isa 9:1, word for word — העם ההלכים בחשך ראו אור גדול ישבי בארץ צלמות אור נגה עליהם. Every content word is Isaiah's, including צלמות (the valley-word of Ps 23:4) and נגה (H5050) — the shining verb this text used at 24:29 of the moon's withheld light. The Isaiah quotations of this chapter (vv. 15-16) are simply Isaiah.

verses.translation: From then onward Yeshua{H3442} began{H2490} to expound{H1875} and to say{H1696}: Turn back in repentance{H8666}, for the kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064} is near{H7138}.

one_way_hebrew: מכאן ואילך — 'from here onward': the Mishnah's own transition formula, a phrase with no biblical or Greek pedigree — pure living Hebrew prose. And the proclamation repeats Yochanan's (3:2) word for word: teacher and forerunner speak one Hebrew sentence — חזרו בתשובה, מלכות שמים — where Greek Matthew's two verses already diverge slightly. לדרוש again: he 'expounds' (see 3:1; 24:14).
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק י״א (Perek 11) begins here.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} went{H1980} along the shore{H8193} of the sea{H3220} of the Galil{H1551} and saw{H7200} two{H8147} brothers{H251} — Shimon{H8095}, who is called{H7121} Simon and called Petros, and Andireah his brother — casting{H7993} their nets{H4365} into the sea, for they were fishermen{H1771}.

one_way_hebrew: The text knows him first as שמעון — the Hebrew tribal name (Gen 29:33) — and gives the Greek forms as bynames, each marked foreign by the scribe's gershayim (סימ״ון, פייט״רוס): the Hebrew name is home, the Greek names are labels.

מכמרת (H4365) — Isaiah's fishing net (Isa 19:8, ופרשי מכמרת); דייגים (H1771) — Jeremiah's fishers (Jer 16:16). The calling scene is furnished from the prophets' own tackle-box — and v. 19 will activate Jeremiah's prophecy.
textual_notes: The printed name-forms carry vowel points (סִימ״וֹן etc.); stripped here, as at 16:13.
Howard's apparatus (4:18): סימון] שימון BG, omit A; שיקרא] הנקרא B, שנקרא CDEFG; הים] ים ADEFG; ואנדיריאה] ואנדריאש A, ואנדריאה BCDEFG; מכמרותיהם] מכמורותיהם BDG.

verses.translation: And he said{H559} to them: Come{H1980} after me{H310}, and I will make{H6213} you fishers{H1771} of men{H376}.

one_way_hebrew: Jer 16:16 — הנני שלח לדיגים רבים... ודיגום ('behold, I send for many FISHERS... and they shall fish them'): YHWH's promised man-fishers, in Jeremiah's own noun (דיגים). In Hebrew, 'fishers of men' completes a standing prophecy; in Greek (ἁλιεῖς ἀνθρώπων) it is a fresh metaphor.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (4:19): מדייגים] דייגים ADEFG; אנשים] מהאנשים AG, מאנשים BDEF; להם] אלהם A.

verses.translation: And they left{H5800} their nets{H4365} in that hour{H8160} and went{H1980} after him{H310}.

greek_deviations: באותה שעה — 'in that HOUR,' the Hebrew time-idiom (as at 24:29's בשעה); Greek εὐθέως ('straightway').

verses.translation: And he turned{H5186} from there{H8033} and saw{H7200} two{H8147} other{H312} brothers{H251}, Yaakov{H3290} and Yochanan{H3110}, brothers, sons{H1121} of Zavdiel{H2068} — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, Zabadao and Zabadah — with their father{H1} in a boat{H591}, preparing{H3559} their nets{H4365}; and he called{H7121} them.

one_way_hebrew: The father is זבדיאל — Zavdiel, a genuine biblical name (1 Chr 27:2; Neh 11:14), 'El has endowed' (זבד) — with the church's worn forms given as the לעז glosses. Greek Ζεβεδαῖος is a transliteration of the Hebrew name; here the Hebrew form stands whole and the Greek forms are the ones needing explanation. And the root זבד returns two verses on (v. 23, זבד טוב) — a resonance only Hebrew carries.
textual_notes: The printed לעז names carry vowel points; stripped.
Howard's apparatus (4:21): בלעז] לעז ACEF, לעז או DG; ואביהם] אביהם עמהם ABDG; באניה] + עמהם EF; the לעז names are spelled variously (זבדאו, זבאדו, etc.).

verses.translation: And they hastened{H4116} and left{H3240} their nets{H4365} and their father{H1}, and went{H1980} after him{H310}.

one_way_hebrew: וימהרו — biblical narrative's haste-verb (Gen 18:6-7; 1 Sam 25:23): Hebrew tells urgency with a converted verb where Greek uses the adverb εὐθέως.
translation_notes: The transcription reads חימהרו; the scan reads וימהרו, corrected here.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} went about{H5437} the land{H776} of the Galil{H1551}, teaching{H3925} their assemblies{H6951} and announcing{H1319} to them the good{H2896} endowment{H2065} — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, maevangelio — of the kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064}, and healing{H7495} every sickness{H2470} and every disease{H4064} among the people{H5971}.

one_way_hebrew: זבד טוב — 'a good endowment': Leah's words at the birth of ZEVULUN, Gen 30:20 — זבדני אלהים אתי זבד טוב. Yeshua walks the land of Zevulun (vv. 13, 15) announcing a זבד טוב, having just called the sons of ZAVDIEL (v. 21): a triple play on one root (זבד) across three verses, invisible in Greek and unplantable by any translator working from it. The scribe glosses the phrase with the church's word — לעז מאוונג״יילייו (evangelio) — exactly as the parallel discourse glosses בשורה at 24:14: the Hebrew term is native; the Greek-Latin term is the visitor.

מדוה (H4064) — Deuteronomy's covenant-curse word (Deut 7:15; 28:60, כל מדוה מצרים — 'every DISEASE of Egypt'): the healer lifts the curse in the curse's own vocabulary. Greek νόσον καὶ μαλακίαν is generic.
קהלות — 'assemblies' (קהל, H6951, the qahal of Israel); Greek συναγωγαῖς transliterates its own institution-word.
textual_notes: The printed loanword carries vowel points; stripped. Howard's English renders it 'mavangeleo.'
Howard's apparatus (4:23): זבד] דבר AB ('the good WORD'), omit EF; חולים] חלי AEF; לעז] בלעז BG; the loanword is spelled variously in the mss.

verses.translation: And the report{H8052} of him went{H1980} into all{H3605} the land{H776} of Syria, and they carried{H5375} to him all the sick{H2470} with all kinds{H4327} of illnesses{H2483}: those seized{H270} by the shedim{H7700}, and those terrified{H1204} by an evil{H7451} spirit{H7307}, and the convulsed{H7493} — and he healed{H7495} them.

one_way_hebrew: The demonology is the Tanakh's, not the Greek's: השדים — shedim (Deut 32:17, יזבחו לשדים; Ps 106:37), where Greek has δαιμονιζομένους; and הנבעתים מרוח רעה — 'terrified by an EVIL SPIRIT': the exact words of Saul's affliction (1 Sam 16:14-15, ובעתתו רוח רעה — בעת H1204 with רוח רעה). The Hebrew classifies the afflicted by Scripture's own cases.
והמתרעשים — 'the convulsed' (רעש, the quaking verb of 24:7): where Greek Matthew has σεληνιαζομένους ('moon-struck'), the Hebrew has shaking, not astrology.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (4:24): מכל] וכל B; וירפא] וירפאו B.

verses.translation: And many{H7227} went{H1980} after him{H310} — from Kapoli and the Galil{H1551}, from Yerushalayim{H3389} and Yehudah{H3063} and beyond{H5676} the Jordan{H3383}.

translation_notes: The ms strings the place-names with gershayim as marked/foreign forms — מקפ״ולי (Decapolis), והג״ליל, מירו״שלם, ויוד״א (the short Aramaic-type form of Yehudah; see 24:16), היר״דן. The transcription reads ויור״א; the scan reads ויוד״א, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (4:25): אחריו] + חרבות ABCDEFG (apparently for חבורות, 'companies'; cf. 5:1); והגליל] הגליל A, ומהגליל G; ועבר] ומעבר A; ויודא] ויהודה A, ומיהודה EFG.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 4 in the Shem Tov Hebrew is built on Deuteronomy quoted by heart. (1) All three answers to the tester are Deut 6-8 cited by incipit and broken off with וגו׳ — 'Not by bread alone, etc.' (4:4 = Deut 8:3); even the Satan quotes Ps 91:11 and stops at וגו׳ (4:6); mss A and D complete the quotations, showing what the abbreviations assume: readers who know the verses. (2) 4:6's base text reads 'If you are ELOHIM, leap down' — no 'son of' (ABDEF/G supply בן) — the second taunt escalates. (3) 4:9: 'all these I will give you if you BARE YOUR HEAD to me' (תפרע, the loosed head of Lev 10:6) — a concrete homage-gesture where Greek has 'fall down and worship'; mss assimilate to תכרע ותשתחוה. (4) 4:10 glosses השטן itself — בלעז שאטאנאס — though Greek Σατανᾶς is a transliteration of the Hebrew: the gloss can only run outward from Hebrew; and the Deut 6:13 quote turns first-person — 'YHWH I will pray to.' (5) 4:12 has Yeshua go to GILGAL (so already 2:22) where Greek reads Galilee. (6) 4:13's Kefar Nachum ('village of Nachum') carries a LATIN gloss — מאריטמה, maritima, 'by the sea' (= Greek's παραθαλασσία); the obscure ראיתה is flagged [?]. (7) 4:15-16 give Isa 8:23-9:1 in Isaiah's own consonants, including the archaic directional ארצה no back-translator could recover. (8) 4:21-23 run a triple play on the root זבד: sons of ZAVDIEL (the biblical name behind 'Zebedee'), the land of ZEVULUN, and the message itself — זבד טוב, Leah's 'good endowment' (Gen 30:20) — glossed לעז מאוונג״יילייו (evangelio), the counterpart of 24:14's בשורה gloss. (9) 4:24's afflicted are classified in the Tanakh's own terms — shedim (Deut 32:17), 'terrified by an evil spirit' (1 Sam 16:14), the convulsed — no 'moon-struck.' (10) 4:11's base ms reads 'the messengers burned him' (וישרפוהו), a פ/ת slip for וישרתוהו 'ministered' — corrected by every other ms. The forty-day fast is Moshe's (Exod 34:28) and Eliyahu's (1 Kgs 19:8), and the ministering messengers close Elijah's scene. Shem Tov's section divisions fall at vv. 1 (Perek 9), 12 (Perek 10), 17 (Perek 11), and 23 (Perek 12).
